prompt: The browser shows a padlock next to the bank's address.
why: The padlock means the connection is encrypted with HTTPS.
trap: It isn't about remembering login; it's about the connection.

prompt: On café wifi, others on the network can't read your password because the connection is encrypted.
why: Encryption keeps traffic private from others on the network. That's HTTPS.
trap: Sessions keep you logged in; encryption keeps it private.

prompt: Visitors see a scary warning because the site's certificate expired.
why: HTTPS relies on a certificate proving the site's identity. An expired one breaks it.
trap: The name still resolved; the security check failed.

prompt: A page loaded over plain http:// is marked 'Not secure'.
why: Without HTTPS, traffic isn't encrypted, so browsers warn you.
trap: It isn't an error code; it's a warning about encryption.

prompt: Encryption stops a network provider from injecting ads into the pages you load.
tells: stops a network provider from injecting ads
why: HTTPS protects against reading and changing traffic in transit.
trap: Nothing about stored copies; it's about the connection.

prompt: The developer gets a free certificate so the site can use https://.
why: A certificate is what lets a site offer HTTPS.
trap: Certificates relate to names, but their purpose is encryption.
